subject: Post-call: Streaming SLOs, measurement probes & harness delivery
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@fastretail.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: daniel.price@fastretail.com
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / discovery call follow-up (streaming SLOs)

Thanks for the quick follow-up, Sofia — good call this morning. I wanted to confirm two things from our side before we dig into any harness artifacts: 1) our primary SLO target for the streaming recommendation flow is p95 <= 120ms and p99 <= 480ms at an average concurrency of 35 (peak 120) and 2) we will need >40 qps sustained for cold-start windows (we log cold-latency separately).

I've attached a small latency sample set from our staging traffic — it includes 30 minutes of traces from yesterday (headers + token counts).

Main asks: can you outline how you plan to measure p95/p99 for streaming (what counts as a token, where you start the timer) and how the harness will treat prefix/KV caching? Also, we want recommended probe prompts that reflect our multi-turn checkout flow.

Alicia
Head of Search & Recommendations
FastRetail, Inc.

[Attachment: staging-latency-sample.csv]

From: sofia_ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@fastretail.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / discovery call follow-up (streaming SLOs)

Alicia — thanks for the sample and for confirming targets. Quick summary of what we'll deliver this week:

- A compact measurement spec (p95/p99 definitions, start/stop metrics for streaming responses, token accounting rules) — spreadsheet attached.
- Prompt pack (jsonl) with canonical multi-turn checkout seeds that mirror your traffic (we'll include deterministic seeds and a small fuzz set).
- Harness run plan: cold-start probes, steady-state concurrency ramps, and a short replay to validate prefix/KV caching behavior.

Short answers to your questions:
- Timer window: for streaming we start timing at the first byte sent back from the model runtime (after request arrives at a serving node). p95/p99 are computed on end-to-end server-observed latencies including our batching queue and network egress inside the region. We will provide both server-only and end-to-end numbers.
- Token accounting: we'll provide tokenization method (BPE variant & tokenizer config) and report both model-tokens and end-user tokens.
- KV/prefix caching: harness includes a toggle to enable/disable KV reuse between sessions. Cold-start runs will explicitly set cache flush.

I'm attaching the slo-probe-specs.xlsx and a first-pass prompt-pack; Ben (cc'd) will call out measurement caveats after this note. Proposed next step: Ben and I run an initial reproducibility probe in our sandbox next Tue and share raw traces for you to review by Wed. Does that timeline work?

— Sofia
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com

[Attachments: slo-probe-specs.xlsx, prompt-pack-v2.jsonl]

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@fastretail.com>, sofia_ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / discovery call follow-up (streaming SLOs)

Alicia — two quick technical clarifications from the runtime side before we lock the probe config:

1) Concurrency model: when you say "average concurrency 35 (peak 120)" we'll run a steady-state phase targeting 35 concurrent active sessions and a separate short peak window at 120 for 3–5 minutes. Important: for streaming p99 you should expect amplification if your sequences are long — we need a sample of sequence-length distribution.

2) Start-of-timer nuance: Sofia's approach (first byte from model) is what we typically use for streaming, but we will also export an "application-start" timestamp you can instrument (so you get an apples-to-apples comparison against your app). For reproducibility we will include the serving-node-id and kernel selection in the trace.

3) Batching & token straights: the harness will log per-token service time and indicate whether a token was served as part of a batched kernel invocation. We'll provide a small script to re-run the same batching cadence locally against your prompt-pack.

Caveat: if you plan to enable quantized variants, p99 behavior can vary across tail latencies — we'll flag those runs separately.

I'll kick off the sandbox probe Tue morning (Oct 6) and post the raw run archive to the Drive link Ben included in the spec workbook.

Ben Carter
Performance Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@fastretail.com>, sofia_ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Harness instructions and reproducibility checklist

Hi Alicia — following Sofia and Ben, attaching the harness-instructions.md with a short reproducibility checklist. Highlights:

- Minimal environment: Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.11, virtualenv, docker-compose for local replay.
- Tokenizer parity: we provide a pinned tokenizer wheel and an example script that prints token counts for each prompt seed.
- Trace artifact layout: run.tar.gz contains traces/{server,client}, metrics/*.prom, prompts/pack.jsonl, and run-config.yaml.
- Repro steps: a) run warmup (50 sessions at low concurrency), b) run cold-start probes (cache flush) x3, c) run steady-state 30m at target concurrency, d) run peak ramp 5m at peak concurrency.

Deliverables after our sandbox run: run.tar.gz, a condensed 2-page readout, and a short Loom showing how to replay locally. We can redact IPs in traces if you want.

Let us know if you prefer we use your staging tokens to hit your endpoint directly (we can also run fully in our sandbox with a replay of your traces).

Thanks — Marissa
Solutions Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: harness-instructions.md]

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@fastretail.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 23:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Streaming SLOs, measurement probes & harness delivery

Appreciate the thorough plan — that timeline works. Quick confirmations from our side:

- We will provide the sequence-length distribution this afternoon (CSV) and a staging token set if you decide to run directly against our staging cluster.
- Please keep quantized runs separate in the readout; we want baseline fp16 runs first.
- We prefer redacted traces in the shared Drive initially. If reproducibility looks good we'll supply staging creds for a direct run.

Next steps: Sofia & Ben to post sandbox run.tar.gz by Wed (Oct 7) morning PST; Marissa to upload harness instructions and Loom. After we review, we'll schedule a 45-minute alignment on Fri to discuss any delta vs our production telemetry.

I'll loop in our infra lead after we review if we need a direct staging run.

Thanks,
Alicia
Head of Search & Recommendations
FastRetail, Inc.
